prompt.provenance_instruction: Answer the following question about Drosophila neuroscience. For every claim you make, state where the information comes from - for example: the specific database, dataset, or tool query you used; the publication (with full citation); or your general training knowledge. If you are uncertain or do not have a source, say so explicitly rather than guessing.

results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. The calyx is closest to the cortex and receives sensory interneuron afferents. The pedunculus is a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes. The mushroom body lobe system consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch, which have different structures at different life stages.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response: There are multiple types of Kenyon cells in the adult Drosophila brain. These include [KCab-c(i)](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049111 "Open KCab-c(i) in Virtual Fly Brain"), [KCab-c](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00110929 "Open KCab-c in Virtual Fly Brain"), [KCg-m](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111061 "Open KCg-m in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Kenyon cell of main calyx](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047926 "Open Kenyon cell of main calyx in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [gamma Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100247 "Open gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"). Additionally, Kenyon cells can be classified into alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells, which are further subdivided into subtypes such as core/surface/posterior, anterior-posterior/middle, and dorsal/main/gamma-s/gamma-t classes. VFB holds [37](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of Kenyon cell") subclasses of [Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain").

results.title: Basic connectivity
results.question: What are the main input neurons to the mushroom body?
results.response: The main input neurons to the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are projection neurons from the antennal lobe and sensory interneuron afferents to the calyx.

results.title: Gene expression
results.question: What neurotransmitter do mushroom body Kenyon cells use?
results.response: Mushroom body Kenyon cells, such as alpha/beta core Kenyon cells, use acetylcholine as their primary neurotransmitter. VFB records show alpha/beta core Kenyon cells as cholinergic, i.e. using acetylcholine.

results.title: Neuroanatomy
results.question: What brain regions does the antennal lobe connect to?
results.response: The [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") connects to the mushroom body and lateral horn. Specifically, the antennal lobe projection neuron sends synaptic output to the mushroom body calyx and/or lateral horn. VFB does not currently hold data on other brain regions that the antennal lobe may connect to.

results.title: Cell count
results.question: Approximately how many neurons are in the adult Drosophila central brain?
results.response:
Approximately more than 125,000 neurons.

**Published neuron-count estimates — adult central brain** (from the literature):

- more than 125,000 neurons (adult Drosophila central brain connectome/model) — A Drosophila computational brain model reveals sensorimotor processing. — PMID 39358519
- ~139,255 neurons (whole adult Drosophila brain) — Neuronal wiring diagram of an adult brain. — PMID 39358518

_VFB has annotated 9,413 neuron types with some part in adult central brain — a curated annotation count, not the biological total._

results.title: Central complex structure
results.question: What are the main components of the Drosophila central complex and what functions are they associated with?
results.response: The main components of the central complex include the ellipsoid body, the fan-shaped body, the paired noduli, the asymmetrical bodies, and the protocerebral bridge. These components are associated with functions such as navigation/orientation, locomotor control, and sleep/arousal or memory-related behaviours.

results.title: Circuit motif
results.question: Describe the dopaminergic input to mushroom body output neurons (MBONs). Which DAN types connect to which MBON types?
results.response: Dopaminergic input to mushroom body output neurons comes from specific types of dopaminergic neurons, including PPL1 and PAM neurons, as well as mushroom body dopaminergic neurons and adult dopaminergic PAM neurons. The connectome data indicates that dopaminergic PPL1 neurons connect to adult dopaminergic neurons. VFB records show that there are various types of dopaminergic neurons providing input to mushroom body output neurons, but the specific connections between different types of dopaminergic neurons and mushroom body output neurons are not fully detailed in the available data.

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response: The [lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111763 "Open lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2 in Virtual Fly Brain") is located in the dorsal area of the lateral cell body rind, with distinct dendritic arbors in each lobula plate layer. It detects looming stimuli and its activity elicits a jump escape response. The LPLC2 visual neuron type connects to the lobula, specifically layers 4 and 5B, with minor processes in layer 5A, and presynaptic sites in layer 4. It projects to an optic glomerulus of the PVLP, anterior to LPLC1 and dorsal to LC4. VFB holds records of approximately 80 of these cells per optic lobe, and they are cholinergic.

results.title: Comparative anatomy
results.question: How does the organisation of the antennal lobe compare between adult and larval Drosophila?
results.response: The organisation of the [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") compares between adult and larval Drosophila in terms of glomerular organization. Both stages are glomerular, but the adult antennal lobe is represented as the more elaborated glomerular neuropil.

results.title: Publications for a circuit
results.question: What publications describe the PPL1 dopaminergic neurons and their role in aversive memory?
results.response: Publications describing the dopaminergic PPL1 neurons and their role in aversive memory include Claridge-Chang et al., 2009, Mao and Davis, 2009, Budnik and White, 1988, and Ren et al., 2016.

results.title: Morphological similarity
results.question: Are there neurons in the Hemibrain dataset that are morphologically similar to the fru+ mAL neurons described in light microscopy studies?
results.response: The Hemibrain dataset contains neurons morphologically similar to the fru+ mAL neurons. VFB records show that neurons similar to the adult fruitless mAL neuron and [adult fruitless aDT-b neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052693 "Open adult fruitless aDT-b neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") are present. However, the exact number of nearest neighbours that are the same cell type as the query is not specified. NBLAST is computed per registered neuron, and the result came from a scored comparison of individual neurons.

results.title: Upstream circuit
results.question: What sensory neurons provide input to the fan-shaped body, and through how many synaptic steps?
results.response: VFB holds [229](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003679,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in fan-shaped body") neuron types with a part in or for the [fan-shaped body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003679 "Open fan-shaped body in Virtual Fly Brain"). The fan-shaped body receives input from various sensory neurons, but the specific sensory neurons and the number of synaptic steps are not specified. VFB does not currently hold data on the exact sensory neurons providing input to the fan-shaped body or the number of synaptic steps involved.

results.title: Bidirectional connectivity
results.question: Are there reciprocal connections between mushroom body output neurons (MBONs) and dopaminergic neurons (DANs)? Which pairs have the strongest mutual connectivity?
results.response: There are reciprocal connections between mushroom body output neurons and dopaminergic neurons. VFB found 5 reciprocal class-level pairs between these two neuron types. The top partners for these connections are not specified, but the target to source weight pairwise connections are 35. The strongest mutual connectivity pairs are not explicitly stated, but the data indicates that there are reciprocal connections with a significant number of partners, with 84 and 98 partner counts mentioned for the two neuron types.

results.title: Pathway tracing
results.question: Trace a pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to the lateral horn. What are the intermediate neuron types and their connections?
results.response: A pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to the lateral horn involves intermediate neuron types, specifically antennal lobe projection neurons. The connections are from olfactory receptor neurons to antennal lobe projection neurons, and then from these neurons to the lateral horn. VFB does not currently hold data on other intermediate neuron types in this pathway.

results.response: The visual system neuron has multiple subtypes. There are more than 1000 matches. The hierarchical organisation of these subtypes is not specified.

results.title: Anatomical containment chain
results.question: Trace the anatomical containment hierarchy from the DA1 glomerulus up to the top-level brain structure. What is each level in the hierarchy?
results.response: The anatomical containment hierarchy from the DA1 glomerulus up to the top-level brain structure is: DA1 glomerulus -> adult antennal lobe -> adult deutocerebrum -> adult cerebrum -> adult central brain -> adult brain. Alternatively, a more specific hierarchy is: DA1 glomerulus -> adult olfactory antennal lobe glomerulus -> adult antennal lobe -> adult deutocerebrum -> adult cerebrum -> adult central brain -> adult brain.

results.response: Neurons that connect the [adult central complex](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003632 "Open adult central complex in Virtual Fly Brain") to the [lateral accessory lobe on L3 CNS template, Wood2018](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_00050314 "Open lateral accessory lobe on L3 CNS template, Wood2018 in Virtual Fly Brain") include [PFL1](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111433 "Open PFL1 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [PFL2_PB4](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111453 "Open PFL2_PB4 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [PFL3_PB7](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111450 "Open PFL3_PB7 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [PFL1_PB1](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111434 "Open PFL1_PB1 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [PFL1_PB7](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111440 "Open PFL1_PB7 in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [PFL1_PB2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111435 "Open PFL1_PB2 in Virtual Fly Brain"). VFB does not currently hold data on the strength of these connections.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior and has a unique anatomy and connectivity. It can be identified by its large descending axon, which is several times larger than any other axon in the cervical connective, and enters the cervical connective via the posterior cerebro-cervical fascicle. The giant fiber neuron descends on the ipsilateral side and has dendritic arborization in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center. It also arborizes in the posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum and gorget. The giant fiber neuron forms electrical synapses with downstream motor and premotor neurons at the inframedial bridge.

Available driver lines for the giant fiber neuron include P{R48A11-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R30C01-p65.AD} and P{R68A06-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R25C08-p65.AD}. Relevant publications on the giant fiber neuron include Thomas and Wyman (1984), Koto et al. (1981), and Namiki et al. (2018).

The giant fiber neuron is classified as a [primary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047097 "Open primary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"). VFB does not currently hold data on the full list of its connectivity partners, but some matching entries include [adult VNC neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00059289 "Open adult VNC neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [thoracic neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00001983 "Open thoracic neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [secondary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047096 "Open secondary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Notch OFF hemilineage neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049540 "Open Notch OFF hemilineage neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [mesothoracic neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00001985 "Open mesothoracic neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), primary neuron, [Notch OFF hemilineage secondary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049542 "Open Notch OFF hemilineage secondary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [prothoracic neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00001984 "Open prothoracic neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Notch ON hemilineage neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049539 "Open Notch ON hemilineage neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [NB2-4 lineage neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00048927 "Open NB2-4 lineage neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Notch ON hemilineage secondary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049541 "Open Notch ON hemilineage secondary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [input/output neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00053396 "Open input/output neuron in Virtual Fly Brain").

results.title: Hypothesis generation
results.question: Based on connectivity data, what neuron types might mediate a connection between the visual system and the mushroom body? Could visual information reach the memory circuit?
results.response: Neuron types that might mediate a connection between the visual system and the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") include projection neurons and visual projection neurons. Adult visual projection neurons to the mushroom body have presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body. This suggests that visual information could reach the memory circuit via these neuron types.

results.title: Novel circuit exploration
results.question: What is the connectivity between thermosensory neurons and the mushroom body? Could temperature information influence memory formation?
results.response: The connectivity between thermosensory neurons and the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") is such that thermosensory projection neurons relay temperature-detecting neurons to higher brain centers, including the mushroom body. This connectivity includes mushroom-body-associated dopaminergic neurons and gamma main Kenyon cells. Temperature information may influence memory formation through this thermosensory influence on mushroom-body memory circuitry. Thermosensory neurons connect to various other neurons, including input/output neurons, projection neurons, and local neurons. VFB does not currently hold data on the full extent of these connections.

results.title: Data availability survey
results.question: I'm interested in studying the subesophageal zone (SEZ). How well-characterised is this region in VFB? What neuron types are annotated, what connectomics data is available, and what genetic tools exist for SEZ neurons?
results.response: The [subesophageal zone](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00051068 "Open subesophageal zone in Virtual Fly Brain") is characterised with available imagery and neuron type annotations. Neuron types with some part in the subesophageal zone can be found by running a query. There are genetic tools for subesophageal zone neurons, including GAL4 drivers and binary/intersectional drivers. VFB holds [4205](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00051068,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in subesophageal zone") genetic tool/expression pattern records for the subesophageal zone, including expression patterns for P{GMR12D05-GAL4}, P{GMR16C05-GAL4}, P{GMR21A07-GAL4}, P{GMR25B07-lexA}, P{GMR54D11-GAL4}, P{GMR65D05-GAL4}, P{GMR87A01-GAL4}, P{VT000003-GAL4}, P{VT000004-GAL4}, P{VT000007-GAL4}, P{VT000008-GAL4}, and P{VT000013-GAL4}. VFB does not currently hold data on the specific connectomics of the subesophageal zone.

results.title: Graph view regression - medulla region connectivity
results.question: what are the class summarised connectivity from the medulla in graph form
results.response: The [medulla](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003748 "Open medulla in Virtual Fly Brain") has connections via tracts or nerves innervating it, as well as neurons with presynaptic and postsynaptic terminals in it. Neurons with some part in the medulla and those with synaptic terminals in the medulla also contribute to its connectivity. The medulla's parts and subclasses, and transgene expression in it, are also relevant to understanding its connectivity.

results.title: Project identity
results.question: What is Virtual Fly Brain and who is it for?
results.response: Virtual Fly Brain is an interactive tool for neurobiologists to explore the detailed neuroanatomy, neuron connectivity, and gene expression of Drosophila melanogaster.

results.title: Website how-to: 3D Viewer
results.question: How do I use the 3D Viewer on the VFB website?
results.response:
To use the 3D Viewer on the VFB website, follow these steps: 
Point and click to select neurons/expression. 
Click and drag with the mouse or use the directional icons to rotate/move. 
Use the zoom icons or scroll with the mouse to zoom in/out. 
The camera icon starts/stops a rotation animation of the scene. 
The sphere icon toggles wireframes on/off.

results.title: Concepts: NBLAST
results.question: What is NBLAST and what does an NBLAST similarity score mean?
results.response: NBLAST is a method used to calculate similarity scores, which represent the morphological similarity between neurons or expression patterns. The similarity scores are calculated using NBLAST. An NBLAST similarity score is a measure of how similar two neurons or expression patterns are in terms of their morphology.

results.question: What are bridging registrations between brain templates in VFB?
results.response: Bridging registrations between brain templates in VFB are transformations to map between different canonical Drosophila templates. results.title: API: REST endpoints
results.question: How can I query Virtual Fly Brain programmatically using the SOLR or Owlery API?
results.response: To query Virtual Fly Brain programmatically, you can use the Owlery API, which provides OWL reasoning services for Virtual Fly Brain's ontologies. The API endpoint is https://owl.virtualflybrain.org/ and it enables Description Logic queries, SPARQL queries with OWL reasoning, and access to multiple knowledgebases. Alternatively, the SOLR Search API provides fast text search and autocomplete functionality for Virtual Fly Brain entities, datasets, and publications.

results.title: API: integrations
results.question: How do I explore Virtual Fly Brain neurons using Navis or pymaid?
results.response:
To explore Virtual Fly Brain neurons, you can use the pymaid library to connect to the VFB CATMAID server and retrieve neurons based on their ID or annotations. You can then use navis to plot the neurons. 
```
import pymaid
import navis

navis.set_pbars(jupyter=False)
pymaid.set_pbars(jupyter=False)

# Connect to the VFB CATMAID server hosting the FAFB data
rm = pymaid.connect_catmaid(server="https://fafb.catmaid.virtualflybrain.org/", api_token=None, max_threads=10)

# Find a neuron from its ID (16) -> this is an olfactory projection neuron
n = pymaid.get_neurons(16)

# Plot CatmaidNeuron with navis
navis.plot3d(n, width=1000, connectors=True, c='k')
```
VFB's documentation does not appear to cover pymaid.

results.title: Anatomy teaching diagrams
results.question: Is there a circuit diagram of the mushroom body available on Virtual Fly Brain?
results.response: There is a schematic representation of the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") available. VFB records show neurons with some part in mushroom body, neurons with synaptic terminals in mushroom body, and parts of mushroom body. The compartmental organisation of the [adult mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003684 "Open adult mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") lobes is described, including how the dendrites of mushroom body output neurons and the axon terminals of dopaminergic neurons tile the lobes into a stereotyped grid of 15 compartments.
